TIM GRIFFIN
                                       ATTORNEY GENERAL


Opinion No. 2026-084

October 30, 2026

The Honorable Scott Flippo
State Senator
Post Office Box 705
Bull Shoals, Arkansas 72619

Dear Senator Flippo:

You recently submitted a request on behalf of a constituent, seeking this Office’s “review and
oversight regarding governance actions taken involving an Arkansas nonprofit corporation,
Hospice of the Ozarks, Inc. and its sole member organization, Baxter County Regional Medical
Center, Inc.”

Specifically, you have asked the following questions:

      1. Were Hospice of the Ozarks, Inc.’s Articles of Incorporation violated or disregarded?

      2. Was the board of Hospice of the Ozarks, Inc. lawfully constituted at the time the bylaws
         were amended?

      3. Were fiduciary duties owed to Hospice of the Ozarks, Inc. and its charitable purpose
         upheld?

      4. Is any corrective or enforcement action warranted under Arkansas law?

RESPONSE

Unfortunately, I am unable to respond to your specific questions. Although I am authorized to
render my opinion to members of the legislature and various state officials regarding matters of
state law, 1 your questions require factual determinations regarding the actions of private nonprofit
corporations, the appointments of directors, the amendment of bylaws, and whether particular




1
    A.C.A. § 25-16-706.

                               BOB R. BROOKS JR. JUSTICE BUILDING
                                   101 WEST CAPITOL AVENUE
                                 LITTLE ROCK, ARKANSAS 72201
 The Honorable Scott Flippo
State Senator
Opinion No. 2026-084
Page 2


individuals complied with fiduciary duties. This Office has consistently declined to resolve
questions of fact in the context of an Attorney General opinion. 2

Additionally, your questions concern the rights, duties, and actions of private parties under specific
corporate governing documents. This Office is not positioned to interpret the specific terms of
contracts and other agreements, nor is it authorized to engage in the interpretation of contracts
entered into by private parties. 3 Addressing the validity or enforceability of such agreements
between private parties, therefore, falls outside of the scope of an Attorney General opinion. Such
matters must instead be addressed by private counsel or by a court. 4

Assistant Attorney General Jodie Keener prepared this opinion, which I hereby approve.

Sincerely,


TIM GRIFFIN
Attorney General




2
    See Ark. Att’y Gen. Ops. 2018-040, 2007-322, 2003-355, 2002-120.
3
  Ark. Att’y Gen. Ops. 2017-032, 2012-044, 2002-340. The Attorney General is statutorily prohibited from engaging
in the private practice of law. A.C.A. § 25-16-701.
4
 This matter was previously the subject of a lawsuit, Joe Dillard, et al. v. Baxter Cnty. Reg. Hosp., Inc., et al., Baxter
County Circuit Court No. 03CV-25-638. That lawsuit has since been dismissed.
